transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

Thank you. Well, what finally scared me into coming in is... after I eat too much, I’ve been making myself throw up in the bathroom. I just do it so I won’t gain weight. I kept thinking it was just a lapse, but it’s gotten to where it isn’t just a one-time mistake anymore. It's happening regularly, and I knew I needed to talk to someone about it.
Could you tell me what your current height and weight are?

I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I haven't stepped on a scale in a little while... I try to avoid looking at the numbers because it just makes me too anxious. And I haven't had my height measured recently either, so I don't really have the exact numbers for you today.
During those times when you eat too much, do you feel a sense of loss of control, like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yes, I do. Once I start during those times, it really feels like I’m on automatic. I'll be sitting there thinking that I need to stop before my husband notices, but... I just keep reaching for one more thing. I really can't seem to stop myself once it begins.
On average, how many times a week are you having these episodes of overeating and making yourself throw up?

Well, for at least the past several months, it's been happening... most weeks, really. I'll have one of those secret eating spells and then go make myself sick afterward. I think it averages out to about once a week, maybe a little more sometimes. I just... I can't honestly call it occasional anymore.
Even without an exact number, would you describe your current weight as noticeably underweight, about average, or higher than average?

I guess I'd say... probably about average. I mean, my clothes still fit mostly the same as they have for a while. I definitely wouldn't say I'm noticeably underweight, but without looking at a scale, I'd just have to guess I'm somewhere around average.
During these eating episodes, roughly how much food would you say you typically eat?

It's a lot. Um, for example, if I come home after a late shift at the store, or maybe after a bridge night with friends, I'll just start eating. I might finish off a leftover casserole, and then eat a batch of cookies I baked, some crackers, and maybe a tub of ice cream, all in one sitting. It's definitely much more food than I would ever put on a plate if someone else was in the room.
How much does your body shape or weight influence how you feel about yourself as a person?

It influences it quite a bit, honestly. Um, for instance, if my skirt feels tight before church, or if I catch my side view in one of the mirrors at the store... it can really just ruin my whole day. I just start feeling like everyone can tell I’ve let myself go, and it makes me feel pretty terrible about myself.
